options.why: solved for $u=e^x$ as $3, 4$ but forgot to take natural logarithms to find $x$
used the linear and constant coefficients of the quadratic equation as arguments
used incorrect negative signs when solving $e^x = 3$ and $e^x = 4$
did not reject the extraneous root $u=-3$, which has no real logarithm
gave the quadratic root $u=7$ rather than solving $e^x = 7$
incorrectly replaced $\ln(-3)$ with $-\ln 3$ instead of rejecting the negative root

questions.solution_text:
Let $u=e^x$.
$u^2 - 4u - 21 = 0$
$(u-7)(u+3) = 0$
$u=7 \text{ or } u=-3$
Since $e^x > 0$ for all real $x$, $e^x = -3$ has no solution.
$e^x = 7 \implies x = \ln 7$

options.why: kept the invalid negative root $u=-3$ instead of discarding it
replaced the positive root $u=\dfrac{1}{2}$ with its reciprocal $2$ and changed the negative root $u=-3$ to $3$ instead of rejecting it, then took natural logarithms
stopped at the substituted variable $u=\dfrac{1}{2}$ without solving for $x$

questions.solution_text:
Let $u=e^x$.
$2u^2 + 5u - 3 = 0$
$(2u-1)(u+3) = 0$
$u = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{ or } u = -3$
Since $e^x > 0$, $u=-3$ is rejected.
$e^x = \dfrac{1}{2} \implies x = \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -\ln 2$

gave the values of $u=\ln x$ instead of exponentiating to find $x=e^u$
took natural logarithms of the roots instead of raising $e$ to the roots

questions.solution_text:
Let $u=\ln x$.
$u^2 - 7u + 10 = 0$
$(u-2)(u-5) = 0$
$u=2 \text{ or } u=5$
$\ln x = 2 \implies x = e^2$
$\ln x = 5 \implies x = e^5$
$x = e^2, e^5$

incorrectly rejected the negative logarithm value $u=-2$, which is valid and gives $x=2^{-2}=\dfrac{1}{4}$
computed $2 \times 4 = 8$ instead of $2^4 = 16$
kept the invalid negative root $u=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, which has no real logarithm
rejected the negative root but stopped at $u=5$ without solving $e^x=5$
changed the negative root $u=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ to $\dfrac{1}{2}$ instead of rejecting it, giving the extra value $\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=-\ln2$

questions.solution_text:
Let $u=e^x$.
$2u^2 - 9u - 5 = 0$
$(2u+1)(u-5) = 0$
$u = -\dfrac{1}{2} \text{ or } u = 5$
Since $e^x > 0$, $u=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ is rejected.
$e^x = 5 \implies x = \ln 5$
